This is an incredibly sweet, chill little game. I've seen some reviews that didn't care for the game because they went in with the wrong expectations, so without spoilers- this is a 2D puzzle platformer with no combat or death system. It's very much a Vibes kind of game, where you're expected to enjoy running around in the beautifully rendered world and experimenting with how to progress through the level in a low-stakes setting. The main game mechanic is the ability to change the in-world seasons, which alters the environment in ways that both aid and hinder progression. This is a fun, inventive tool, and it only adds to the artistic direction by effectively having four versions of each map. If you're after a highly story driven game, or a puzzle platformer like Ori that's punishingly difficult, this game isn't what you're after. But if you want to just decompress and enjoy a beautiful world and pretty ambient music while making a cute fox hop around, absolutely go for it.

Сезонс афтер Фол — это как если бы твоя депрессия решила стать лисой и побегать по лесу, где каждый сезон — это новый этап "я не справлюсь".
Ты — рыжая лиса, которая прыгает по веткам, меняет погоду и... ну, в общем, просто бегает. Без оружия, без врагов — только ветер, листья и твоя грусть.
Геймплей? Прыгай, скользи, меняй время года — и через десять минут ты уже не играешь, а просто дышишь в такт дождю.
Графика — как будто кто-то нарисовал осень, зиму, весну и лето одним махом: всё мягкое, всё живое, всё пахнет мокрой землёй.
Минус: если ты хочешь экшена — иди в другую игру. Здесь ты просто... существуешь.
Плюс: когда ты наконец добираешься до конца — это как если бы ты обнял свою тоску и сказал "ну, ладно, пойдём дальше".Вердикт: 9/10. Запусти вечером, без музыки — и почувствуй, как мир становится тише.

While most platformers challenge you to master complex combat mechanics, Seasons after Fall invites you to master the passage of time. Players on Steam describe the game not as a simple gaming challenge, but as an “interactive storybook,” where you are an agile fox with the magical power to change the seasons at will. It’s the kind of experience where there are no enemies to kill you and no “Game Over” screens, with the focus entirely on exploration, environmental puzzle-solving, and immersion.
The focus of the community’s praise is undoubtedly the art direction. Everything feels hand-painted, with a color palette that morphs spectacularly before your eyes: winter freezes over lakes to open up new paths, while spring sprouts plants that serve as platforms. This seasonal change mechanic is seamlessly tied to a soundtrack performed by a string quartet, which many players say is "one of the best in indie history", managing to induce or stay in deep silence.
However, recent "Mixed" reviews (as seen in your screenshot) draw attention to one important aspect: the game's pace. While the universe is charming, some users mention that the game involves quite a lot of backtracking (repeated paths through the same areas), which can become slightly monotonous for those used to fast-paced action. It's a game that asks you to slow down, observe and enjoy the atmosphere, being more of a contemplative "puzzle-puzzler" than a precision platformer.
In conclusion, Seasons after Fall is the perfect recommendation for evenings when you want to escape the stress of everyday life. It is proof that games can be art in motion, offering a short but memorable journey that will remain etched in your mind through its unparalleled aesthetics.

If I could I would give a neutral review of this game, because it's not really a bad game, so I feel kind of bad giving it a negative review. However, I feel like if I have to choose between recommending it and not, I personally would not recommend it to my friends.

I'll start with the pros:

- Pretty good music
- Decent art style
- Ambience is kind of pleasant sometimes

Here's what I didn't like:

- The first half of the game feels like a drawn out tutorial
- "Puzzles" are not that interesting, and often more tedious than challenging. Nothing is that hard to solve, it feels like a lot of trial-and-error and exploring around an area
- I found myself often wanting the game to be over, because I wasn't really enjoying it
- Running back and forth to places I've already been, with a few additional mechanics is just boring
- The story/narrative attempts to be very deep and poetic, but it's just kind of nonsensical and confusing. Seems like it takes a lot of words to say basically nothing.

It says I've played for 11 hours, that's only because I left the game on pause for hours at a time while I did other things. Realistically, it should take only 5-7 hours to complete, but I feel like even that is more time than I wanted to spend playing this game. I finished it just because after 2-3 hours in, I knew there wasn't much farther to go. But if I could go back, I would never have started it.

Le jeu est très beau, la musique très belle. Mais après les premières heures on se lasse très vite.
Il n'y a pas beaucoup de maps, et le jeu nous les fait faire et refaire beaucoup trop de fois. Surtout, on a aucun accès à une vue d'ensemble, pas d'affichage de carte, alors certains lieux sont un enfer à traverser car on se perd beaucoup trop facilement. Obligé de finir le jeu avec des solutions car les indications sont très mauvaises... 
Le renard saute avec un léger délais, ce qui est vraiment dommage quand on est sur un jeu de plateforme. Idem, le système de changement de saison prend vraiment trop de temps selon certains passages, on devient vite saoulé par toutes ces petites secondes perdues. 
L'histoire est simple, un peu trop même... La fin laisse une sensation d'inachevé. On perd un personnage important quasiment à la moitié du jeu sans jamais avoir de nouvelles comme s'il avait été oublié. 
La première fois que j'y ai joué j'avais abandonné. Récemment je m'y suis remise car j'avais tout oublié et je comprends pourquoi j'ai laissé tombé il y a des années de ça. Je l'ai fini à 100% pour le principe mais je n'y toucherais plus.

Alors l'avis est mitigé,
On a une belle DA, on concept de puzzle plateformer 2D original, un doublage français dont on reconnait aisément nos formidables comédiens de doublage made in France.

Mais malheureusement le jeu est littéralement ruiné par la maniabilité du renard, j'ai l'impression de conduire un semi remorque. les commandes sont lourdes, les sauts pas précis, un délai trop long entre le moment où j'appuie sur le bouton et le moment où le renard saute. Pour un plateformer 2D c'est le comble. 
5h pour finir le jeu, avec une bonne maniabilité, le jeu se finirait en 3 ou 4. Rien de plus frustrant que de refaire 4-5 fois un passage de plateformes parce que soit le renard ne saute pas quand on appuie, soit il fait un demi saut.
Apres on tourne un peu en rond aussi, On actionne un élément quelque part qui fait apparaitre un truc, on ne sait pas vraiment où se trouve ce fameux truc, on a l'impression qu'il apparait à droite de nous alors qu'en fait, c'est à gauche.

Pourtant, j'ai bien aimé le concept mais la maniabilité m'a parfois frustré alors que c'est un jeu qui est sensé être chill.

Seasons After Fall is a platformer and puzzle game with a stunning visual aesthetic. In my opinion, it’s a very original game when it comes to its puzzle-solving mechanics, which, as the name suggests, are based around the seasons. One of the most common complaints I see in reviews is that the areas feel repetitive and that you never know where to go. First of all, one of the game’s main ideas is exploration. While you do revisit areas, there are always new puzzles in them, making each visit feel different. The game does give you hints about where to go; I think the real problem is that people don’t think enough. Overall, it’s a very good platformer and puzzle game, and I recommend it if you want to have a good time.

Seasons After Fall is a beautifully crafted indie puzzle-platformer that offers a unique and tranquil journey through a mystical forest. Developed by Swing Swing Submarine and published by Focus Entertainment, the game invites players to step into the paws of a clever fox imbued with the magical ability to control the changing seasons. The premise centers on restoring balance to the natural world by recovering lost fragments of each season, a narrative woven subtly through the game's environments and atmospheric cues rather than overt storytelling. This focus on exploration and harmony with nature gives the game a calm and reflective tone, setting it apart from more conventional, combat-heavy titles.

The game's artistic design is one of its most striking features. Every scene feels hand-painted, filled with lush detail and vibrant colors that shift dramatically with the seasons. From the bright, warm hues of autumn leaves swirling in the wind to the stark, icy blues of winter, each seasonal transition is visually stunning and plays a vital role in gameplay. The player’s ability to switch between seasons dynamically alters the landscape, unlocking new paths, freezing lakes to walk on, or causing plants to bloom and grow. This mechanic is not just clever but deeply satisfying, encouraging players to experiment and observe the environment closely to solve puzzles and progress. The world feels alive and reactive, inviting players to slow down and savor its beauty.

Accompanying the gorgeous visuals is an evocative and soothing soundtrack, performed live by a string quartet. The music perfectly complements the game's peaceful atmosphere, enhancing the emotional weight of the journey without ever overpowering the experience. Ambient sounds like the rustling of leaves, gentle wind, and distant animal calls further immerse players in this magical woodland setting. This careful sound design contributes to the game's meditative quality, making it feel like a brief but deeply meaningful escape into nature.

Despite its many strengths, Seasons After Fall is not without its limitations. One of the most notable drawbacks is the game's relatively short length; many players report completing the main story in about four to six hours. While the experience is rich and rewarding, this brevity can leave some wanting more, especially those who enjoy longer or more complex puzzle-platformers. Additionally, the game’s minimalistic approach to guidance means players might occasionally feel directionless or stuck without clear objectives or hints. This lack of hand-holding can frustrate some, though it also encourages exploration and problem-solving through observation and experimentation.

Replay value is somewhat limited as well. Beyond the main quest, there are collectibles scattered throughout the forest, such as hidden flowers and dreams, which encourage thorough exploration. However, these collectibles serve mainly as achievements rather than adding substantial new content or challenges. Once players have completed the game, there is little incentive to return, as the puzzles and season-switching mechanics do not evolve or expand. For players seeking a deeper or more extended engagement, this might be disappointing.

Nevertheless, Seasons After Fall excels in delivering a charming and serene experience that resonates emotionally with many players. Its emphasis on nature, subtle storytelling, and seamless integration of seasonal mechanics make it a standout among indie puzzle games. The game's peaceful pace and beautiful world provide a perfect escape for those looking to unwind and appreciate thoughtful game design and artistry. It is a title that invites contemplation rather than competition, making it ideal for players who enjoy games as a form of artistic expression and quiet exploration.

In sum, Seasons After Fall is a lovingly crafted game that shines through its atmosphere, art, and innovative use of seasonal shifts. While it may not satisfy those craving hours of complex gameplay or fast-paced action, it offers a refreshing alternative — a brief but immersive journey into a magical forest filled with wonder and subtle storytelling. For anyone who appreciates calm, beauty, and the gentle challenge of nature-inspired puzzles, this game is a memorable and worthwhile experience.

It took me a few days to finish the game. And while it required patience and a steady mindset, in the end I was glad I stayed with it, because I found exactly what I was looking for: a heartfelt, beautiful, and touching adventure.
After finishing, there’s a sense of calm left behind, tinged with a gentle sadness, like a quiet melody slowly fading away.
I sincerely recommend [i]Seasons after Fall[/i] to anyone who enjoys exploring new worlds, listening to evocative music, and solving puzzles at a slow, almost meditative pace.

При определённых достоинствах [b]«Seasons after Fall»[/b], проходить игру до конца пришлось через силу, хватило терпения всё же её «добить», только чтобы окончательно укрепиться в своём мнении, что игра посредственная.

Да, рисованная графика просто чарует. И музыка волшебная. В начале игра действительно вызывает восхищение. И двое персонажей, которые в игре говорят, озвучены недурно. Но в самом главном — в собственно игровом процессе — игра не удовлетворяет нисколько. Игра позиционируется как пазл-платформер. В части платформера ничего особенного — ну да, бегаем, прыгаем, но каких-то вызовов, механик завязанных на преодолении препятствий, короче говоря «паркура», здесь нет. Разве что считать вызовом слегка неадекватное управление, но привыкнуть можно. С пазлами же всё совсем печально. На всю игру 2-3 момента, где требуется хотя бы на секунду задуматься, а что собственно делать и в какой последовательности, чтобы решить поставленную задачу. Весь остальной игровой процесс — беготня в поисках чего-нибудь, в процессе которой максимально неизобретательно эксплуатируется паттерн «смените сезон на такой-то, чтобы активировать предмет», причём беготня пусть и по красиво нарисованным, но крайне однообразным локациям, которые быстро приедаются. И не всегда очевидно, а что собственно нужно искать, но куда чаще возникает вопрос где искать, ведь карты нет, а когда что-то в игровом мире меняется, показывают лишь короткую кат-сцену, и только по ней попробуй теперь угадать, куда двигаться дальше. И если, скажем, в метроидваниях шныряние туда-сюда по карте разбавляется боёвкой, побочными задачами и банальным исследованием в поисках ништяков, то здесь ничего такого нет (кроме поиска опциональных штук для достижений, не влияющих на игровой процесс). Пойди туда — не знаю куда, принеси то — непонятно зачем. Сюжет и лор в игре как бы присутствуют, но поражать они могут разве что непроработанностью и бессмысленностью. [i]«In this world, nothing ever starts and nothing ever ends (В этом мире ничего никогда не начинается и никогда не заканчивается),»[/i] — сообщает нам мишка в конце, видимо говоря о смысловом содержании игры, точнее его отсутствии.

Итог: душно, очень скучно. С такой графикой и музыкой создателям оставалось бы лишь подойти с умом к сценарию и можно было бы сделать классный мультфильм. А получилась унылая игра.

Seasons After Fall is a beautiful game with lovable fox and a sweet story. The art and the music are lovely and the voice acting is professionally done. The game has full controller support which was appreciated because I currently have my right hand (including 3 fingers) in a cast. I think this would be a tough game to play with a keyboard and mouse, even with two hands!

This a very complicated landscape that can be quite frustrating at times. The absence of a map and the inability to see more than the current screen compound your ability to feel hopelessly lost. Thus, prepare to peek at a guide or to practice patient exploration.

The game auto-saves at regular intervals to a single slot. Achievements are not truly missable, as you can circle back to take care of missing tasks or collectibles. The only exception to this may be the requirement of finding all 4 dreams to activate the full ending.

There is a lot of platforming required and no instructions in-game. The mechanics of the 4 seasons are tough initially but become intuitive after awhile. The good news is that there are no time limits and nothing to chase you.

All in all, a very cool but complex game. I recommend it to those who don't mind A LOT of running and jumping and are not in a hurry. Those who enjoy games like Neva and Gris (sans the monsters) should feel right at home in Seasons After Fall.

[b]玩法方面，[/b]展现出的极简主义，既没有战斗也没收集，甚至没有UI。小狐狸除了跳就是叫，你永远可以相信小狐狸的跳跃能力，而比较整蛊的是26个字母按键，23个对应的都是狐狸叫。过程中通过控制季节变换来改变场景，以达目的，感觉算不上解谜，顶多算机关。一路上有声线活泼又好听的旁白为玩家打消寂寞感，流程大约6个小时，全成就也十分容易

[b]地图方面，[/b]以庇护所为中心，四个角落方向各为春夏秋冬，而一个季节其实就只有一条路，但作为2D游戏来说，它每个房间做得非常宽敞，让人不禁怀疑自己是否走错，有无遗漏。大、小提琴的配乐很好听，但一路上基本没有BGM，只有鸟啼虫鸣声，草木的摩擦声，和我CPU的风扇声。。。

[b]剧情方面，[/b]有点童话低龄向，对成年人来说或许有点幼稚，但对小孩子倒是刚刚好。中文流几乎都把游戏名译为“秋后的季节”，其实有点偏颇嘞。游戏中没有哪个季节占比很大，不论是秋还是秋后的冬，都并不具有代表性。相对的，Fall在此更像是一种衰落，丧失的抽象意义而非单纯的秋季。至于四季如何衰落又能否复兴，就自己去探寻答案吧~

想了想，我若是拥有控制四季的超能力。。。好像也没多厉害啊！即使控制了季节，一切也不是一蹴而就的。不过会想把季节固定在夏天，只待在空调房和海边，一周吃十次冰激凌，既不用担心花粉过敏，也不用怕感冒着凉，我永远喜欢夏天(๑˃̵ᴗ˂̵)و✧




P.S.以防你对这游戏没什么兴趣，但又好奇[url=https://cdn.steamusercontent.com/ugc/16018490360627773964/27F462B1A8146D13AEBFD78629FD4BE544571383/]狐狸的叫声[/url]

P.P.S.无意冒犯任何喜欢它的人，但《What Does The Fox Say》这首歌当初给我的感觉是[spoiler]神…神经病啊！！[/spoiler]直到现在又去听了一下还是让我头皮发麻。。。

Wie bekomme ich meine 9 Stunden verlorene Lebenszeit zurück? Das Spiel ist kurz gesagt, die Zeit nicht Wert. Ich mochte die beiden vorherigen Spiele des Entwicklers "Swing Swing Submarine" sehr gerne und habe diese immer hoch gelobt. Ich hatte den Entwicklern bei beiden Titeln sogar ein eMail geschrieben wie toll ich diese Spiele fand (für mich waren das perfekte Spiele!)... Seasons after Fall ist das 3. Spiel des Entwicklers und ja, es sieht gut aus. Punkt. Damit hätten wir das Positive mal hinter uns und um nicht noch mehr Lebenszeit zu verschwenden:

Die Steuerung ist unverständlicherweise der größte Mist der mir jemals untergekommen ist. Jede Bewegung hat einen Inputdelay von mindestens einer halben Sekunde (sowohl mit "Kabel", als auch per Funk). DH. jeder Sprung muss im Voraus gedrückt werden und wehe man wechselt die Richtung und springt gleichzeitig, dann gibt es gefühlt den doppelten Inputdelay... Das muss eine bewusste Gameplayentscheidung gewesen sein, denn beide anderen Spiele des Entwicklers bestechen mit einer extrem guten und präzisen Steuerung (bei Verwendung des/der gleichen Gamepads!). - Ich möchte nicht wissen wie viele Gamepads bei diesem Spiel ihr Leben lassen mussten!

Ehrlich gesagt, weiß ich noch immer nicht genau was meine Aufgabe in dem Spiel war... Das ganze Spiel war ein zugegeben hübsches, aber völlig plan- und orientierungsloses hin und her laufen. Das ist zwar schon schlimm genug, aber das ständige wiederholen und Backtracking war noch grausamer... Es gibt teilweise Abkürzungen, aber nur in eine Richtung. Einmal eine falsche Abkürzung genommen und schon geht´s wieder ans Backtracking... Ich war so planlos, dass ich zwei der etwas größeren Rätsel zufällig gelöst habe, obwohl das zu diesem Zeitpunkt weder meine Aufgabe war, noch ich davon wusste!?

Das ganze Spiel verursacht Frust und Aggressivität, weil man bereits gelöste (Mini-)Rätsel immer und immer wieder neulösen muss zB. um Hindernisse wiederholt zu überwinden, sei es wegen dem plan- und orientierungslosen hin und herlaufen, dem Backtracking oder einen zweiten, dritten, vierten, ... Versuch, wenn die Steuerung wieder versagt hat. 

Ich bin froh das ich dieses Spiel nie wieder angreifen muss.

Le début est intéressant, et le maniement des saisons pour résoudre les puzzles est bien conçu. Mais au bout de deux heures, toutes les saisons sont réunies et s’entame alors un (très) longue phase de nouveaux puzzles plus difficiles. Passe encore. C'est après que le jeu devient vraiment agaçant et ennuyant. Les objectifs ne sont pas clairs, le scénario assez basique et enfantin, et le gameplay devient vite répétitif. Les doublages sont en revanche d'excellente qualité et l'OST aussi bien que (beaucoup) trop absente. J'ai personnellement vraiment essayé d'aller au bout du jeu, même si ça ne m'amusait pas, mais j'ai finalement abandonné à la toute fin, ou c'était presque une punition de jouer au jeu.
 Bref : je ne le conseille pas, bien que la direction artistique soit franchement jolie, le jeu en soit manque cruellement de structuration.
